summary.prose: This Story adds one conversion command, repo.convert, that brings a repository onto the common artifact model: a planner computes every change from the stored files (a preview writes nothing), an applier runs the rules in a fixed order, a verifier compares a delivery snapshot computed before from the legacy stamps with one read afterwards by the delivery reader, and the version marker is written last. Heads are written by a conversion-owned migration write that keeps each head's revision number, status and approval as stored, because writing them through ArtifactStore would move revisions and return approved heads to draft. The same Story then retires the legacy approval and review stamps, the body.feedback writers and the s6 to s8 fallbacks, so the repository ends on one code path.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): a shared artifact envelope with typed payloads, stored as a head file plus two append-only sidecar files whose lines carry the owning artifact id, behind a single identity module, with one upfront conversion and no compatibility code. The envelope carries identity, description, parent, references, a typed lifecycle (revision, approval, review, signoffs, staleness, status) and a tracker binding or attachments; the change log and feedback are separate append-only line files; each existing artifact type shrinks to a payload codec and a renderer. Tracker comment reading and attaching are added to the port and implemented for the GitHub adapter only.

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactIdScheme
consumedContracts.purpose: The single place artifact ids are made and recognised: the existing hierarchical typed ids extended for Epic, Story, Task, the Tasks file and diagrams, one story and task form, the folder-name date source, and the functional-requirement id helpers that live in id.ts today.

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactEnvelope
consumedContracts.purpose: The common shape of every stored entity and the one reader and writer for it, with References and namespaced Actors.

consumedContracts.name: HistoryRecords
consumedContracts.purpose: The change log entry and the Feedback entry shapes, the persisted sidecar record that carries the owning artifact id, and the append and read API, including how an update says which feedback it addressed.

consumedContracts.name: Lifecycle
consumedContracts.purpose: The typed lifecycle structures, the ten statuses and their transitions, the revision and content-hash rule, the completion roll-up and the conflict check against the log tail.

consumedContracts.name: SidecarStorage
consumedContracts.purpose: How an artifact is stored: the head file and the two append-only line files shared by a Tasks file, their location, the merge rule, the per-artifact filtering and the read-time ordering and de-duplication.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface ArtifactFiles { head: string; log: string; feedback: string }
interface SidecarStore { filesOf(id: string): ArtifactFiles; appendRecord<E>(file: string, record: SidecarRecord<E>): Promise<void>; readRecords<E>(file: string, artifactId: string): Promise<E[]>; mergeAttributes(): string[] }

consumedContracts.name: TrackerBinding
consumedContracts.purpose: The typed binding between a lifecycle artifact and its tracker issue, the attachments of supporting artifacts, and the tracker port operations to read comments and attach, implemented for the GitHub adapter.

consumedContracts.name: TaskSet
consumedContracts.purpose: The Tasks file of a plan: the Task artifacts, their ids, and how a re-plan is brought into line without reusing an id.

consumedContracts.name: RepoSchemaVersion
consumedContracts.purpose: The repository-level marker that records whether a repository has been converted, so the conversion is repeatable and the new tools refuse an unconverted repository.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface RepoSchema { version: number; convertedAt?: string }
interface RepoSchemaGate { read(repo: string): RepoSchema; require(repo: string, atLeast: number): { ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string } }

boundary.internal: The conversion command: previews, repeats, back-fills history, renames standalone S001 to s1 rewriting the references it can with no alias, creates Epic, Story and Task artifacts for what exists, verifies through the delivery reader, and sets the repository version. Private to this Story are the per-type conversion mappings and the verification report.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The id module and its removal of the second scheme: the folder-name formatter moved into the path scheme, the date source fixed to the epic's creation time, the functional-requirement id helpers and their callers moved with stored FR ids staying valid, issue titles switched to the artifact id, and the delivery module's ordinals. The old issue-body marker is not read. Private to this Story are the exact text of the issue title and the relocation of the helpers.

The envelope model, the one reader and writer, the History API and the sidecar record shape as a contract, and the repository version marker. Private to this Story are the head-file schema, the per-type payload codec registry and how the old per-type read functions delegate to the reader.

The lifecycle rules: status transitions, the revision and content-hash computation, the staleness record, the completion roll-up and the integrity check against the log tail on approve, review and complete. Private to this Story are the hash canonicalisation and how a roll-up is cached or recomputed.

The physical sidecar storage: file layout, the merge attributes for the line files, per-artifact filtering, read-time ordering and de-duplication, and the write order of log entry before head with the repair of a log that is ahead of its head. Private to this Story are the line format and the file naming beside a head.

People-facing feedback: adding feedback and replies from a client, listing open feedback, the addresses rule at revision time, and the per-user identity declaration with alias linking. Private to this Story are the identity file format and the display of linked identities.

The typed binding and attachments, the tracker port additions implemented for GitHub, the retry of pending links and posts, and the switch of unit-issue bookkeeping to the binding. Private to this Story are the permalink construction and the retry bookkeeping.

Task artifacts: creation of the Tasks file and the Task issues at plan approval, direct edits of a Task's own content with local re-approval, refusal of structural edits, and the re-plan reconciliation. Private to this Story are the diff of a Task against the new plan and the build-round recording in a Task's history.

Comment sync: reading human comments into feedback at implement, validate or on request, classifying a revision request or a suggestion from the first line, and posting feedback once. Private to this Story are the first-line commands, the derived since point and the filter for the framework's own posts.

nonFunctional.performance: Reading an artifact reads its head; the log tail is read only on approve, review and complete, and counts, open feedback and status are computed on read. The delivery loader still reads each artifact once. Loading a repository of about a thousand artifacts must stay within twice today's load time on the same machine.
nonFunctional.security: Gates use the live tracker identity only; declared aliases are never trusted for a decision. The identity file is local and read for attribution. Tracker comments are read through the existing gh path of the GitHub adapter, with no new credential and no direct REST call.
nonFunctional.observability: Every state change appends a change log entry with actor, operation and, where relevant, revision and status; a conflict, a log-ahead-of-head repair, a failed attach and a pending link are logged and surfaced in the unit's result, not hidden.
nonFunctional.durability: Heads are replaced atomically as today; sidecar lines are append-only and de-duplicated by (artifactId, entry id) so a repeated append is harmless; a write appends its log entry before it replaces the head so a failure between the two leaves a detectable, repairable gap; the conversion is one commit, repeatable, and reverts with one git revert.

dataModelChanges.details: { changes: ConversionChange[]; renames: { from: string; to: string }[]; unmapped: UnmappedField[]; problems: { file: string; reason: string }[]; legacyAttachComments: { issue: string; commentId: string }[]; snapshot: DeliverySnapshot }. snapshot is the before-snapshot from legacyDeliveryView. ConversionChange is a union keyed by rule (rename-id, stamp-epic-created-at, convert-amendment, migrate-head, convert-feedback, create-epic, create-story, create-tasks, move-binding, move-story-history, strip-legacy-field, relabel-issue); each names the artifact id and the stored state that makes the rule apply.

Deterministic ids: migrated-<artifact id> is the revision-bearing entry (operation create when the artifact has no log, update otherwise; revision { number: the head's meta.revision, contentHash: the hash of the converted content }; actor insrc:migration; outcome.data.kind 'migrated'; timestamp = the conversion's clock, so it is the last revision-bearing entry and checkIntegrity compares the head against it). migrated-<artifact id>-approve, -reject and -mark-stale are revision-less entries carrying the legacy fact (original time from the stamp, actor legacy:unknown, status from/to). migrated-<artifact id>-review is a revision-less 'review' entry whose outcome.data holds { kind: 'review', report: the stored ReviewReport, resolutions: reviewResolutions }. An entry is appended only when its id is not found in History.log.

status, approval, review and stale are computed from meta.approvedAt, rejectedAt, rejectReason, reviewOverride, staleAckedAt and meta.review with reviewResolutions applied (as effectiveReviewVerdict decides), bound to the head's current meta.revision; a review dated before the revision is not bound to it. The revision number, status and approval are kept as stored; revision.contentHash is contentHash of the converted description, body and citations. lifecycle.review keeps verdict, counts, party and at, and its report is a Reference { entityId: the artifact id, type: 'change-log-entry', relation: 'reviews', fragment: the review entry id }. Current behaviour kept (invariant): approval and review bind to a revision number, not to a hash, so a changed hash does not unbind them (src/workflow/storage.ts, src/workflow/artifact-core/lifecycle.ts).

The full ReviewReport (findings, claims, model, reviewedBy) and the resolutions leave meta.review and meta.reviewResolutions and live in the outcome.data of the artifact's 'review' change-log entry; new reviews written by persistReview do the same, and a later resolution is a further log entry with outcome.data.kind 'review-resolution'. Readers use readReviewReport: src/workflow/review/resolve.ts (effectiveReviewVerdict), src/workflow/tracker-auto.ts (readReview, 377-381), src/workflow/delivery/gate.ts (103), src/workflow/delivery/currency.ts (80, 181), src/workflow/review/party.ts (reviewerPartyOf), src/workflow/gates.ts (641, 746, 889), src/workflow/artifact-content.ts.

A head is written by writeMigratedHead, not by ArtifactStore.write: the store's content write moves meta.revision and returns the head to draft when the content hash changes (src/workflow/storage.ts, prepareArtifactWrite), and the conversion changes the body (it strips body.feedback and rewrites ids). The migration write sets meta.envelope and meta.lifecycle, strips the legacy fields, keeps meta.revision, and writes by writeAtomic after the log entries; it does not touch the sc2 store contract.

dataModelChanges.entity: meta legacy stamps: writers and gates
dataModelChanges.details: Move to LifecycleService (apply, updateContent) and delete the stamp: src/workflow/gates.ts (approveArtifactByJsonPath, reject and ack-stale gates, STAMP_KEYS, mirrorLegacyReview, headConflict becomes the full log check), src/workflow/review-decision.ts, src/workflow/review/resolve.ts, src/workflow/bugfix/stamp.ts, src/workflow/bugfix/mount.ts, src/workflow/artifacts/issue.ts, src/daemon/tasks-sync.ts, src/daemon/index.ts, src/workflow/runners/build/completion-record.ts, src/workflow/runners/build/standalone-record.ts, src/workflow/runners/build/range-base.ts. LifecycleService becomes mandatory on WorkflowApproveRequest and ReviewArtifactOpts.

Read the lifecycle (status, approval, review, stale) instead; ordered before the conversion is first run: src/workflow/delivery/load.ts (approvalOf), src/workflow/delivery/gate.ts, src/workflow/delivery/currency.ts, src/workflow/delivery/types.ts, src/workflow/pending.ts, src/workflow/bugfix/admit.ts, src/workflow/chain.ts, src/workflow/artifact-content.ts, src/workflow/artifact-core/completion-evidence.ts, src/workflow/runners/tracker/context.ts, src/workflow/tracker/conventions.ts, src/workflow/types.ts, src/shared/access.ts, src/mcp/server.ts, src/cli/services/workflow.ts, src/workflow/tracker-auto.ts, src/workflow/review/party.ts, src/daemon/workflow-rpc.ts, src/workflow/artifact-write-inventory.ts (the findings.ts entry changes with persistReview).

Each flat AMD file becomes a { meta, body, citations } head with a lifecycle from its own approval and rejection stamps; approveAmendment and the other amendment functions move to the head shape and the lifecycle in the same change.

persistReview replaces the three copies of inspect, head conflict check, fix, stamp, lifecycle record and markdown. src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/findings.ts, which today stamps meta.review with a meta-only write and records nothing on the lifecycle, joins it, so HLD and LLD design reviews are bound to the lifecycle without the approval-time mirror. The lifecycle record comes before the markdown; a failure names the step.

Each entry becomes a Feedback line through convertLegacyFeedback and the decision of each batch the outcome of a change log entry; the field is stripped by the migration write from DEF, HLD, LLD and PLAN heads. appendFeedback, appendFeedbackBatch and the tool artifact_feedback_append are removed; the companion headers and the delivery text read FeedbackService threads. convertLegacyFeedback changes: actor id (namespaced id kept, else legacy:<slug>, author text in actor.properties.name), kind by decision, foreign target.file in anchor.section.

epicRef and storyRef(s) move to the binding of the EPIC and STORY head they describe (move-binding, limited to Define to EPIC and LLD to STORY); taskRefs and units for Tasks are moved by TaskSets.createFromPlan alone (no second writer). All are removed with their readers: src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts (older-refs rebind, Task branch of recordUnit, bindingHome's Plan fallback), refs.ts, resolve.ts, sync.ts, link.ts, conventions.ts, src/workflow/orchestrator.ts, chain.ts, questions.ts, storage.ts, tracker-auto.ts, the artifact renderers define.ts, hld.ts, lld.ts, tracker.ts, the tracker runners context.ts, index.ts, schemas.ts, runners/build/changed-files.ts, code-review/grounding.ts, tasks/task-set.ts, daemon/steps/build-step/render.ts.

The move-story-history rule copies, for each Story, the LLD's attachments, its tracker:<comment id> feedback lines and its feedback-post receipts to the STORY head (sidecar lines are append-only, so the LLD keeps its copies as history; feedback ids de-duplicate). artifactOfUnit in src/workflow/tracker/comment-sync.ts then answers the STORY head, so the sync reads and posts there. The unmarked pre-s8 'Attached ...' comments are not rewritten: when a tracker port is supplied the plan lists them in legacyAttachComments and the report names them.

One EPIC head per Define and one STORY head per Story in it, created with the pass-through codecs; parent chain Epic, Story, LLD; the Epic binding moves from the Define's envelope and the Story binding from the LLD's, with their attachments; status by rollUp. Folders under docs/epics keep their names.

TaskSets.createFromPlan runs for each approved PLAN that has no TASKS head (plan row ids kept); it already moves the Plan's Task tracker record onto each head's binding (src/workflow/tasks/task-set.ts, doc at lines 140-146), so the conversion adds no Task-record writer. One revision-less build round (kind build-round) is back-filled per BUILD task result that passed. bindingHome's Plan fallback and taskBuildPassed's BUILD-record branch are then deleted.

writeRepoSchema writes .insrc/schema.json as { version: 2, convertedAt } by a temporary file and a rename, only after every head is clean. The RepoSchema shape is the sc8 shape unchanged; this Story is the only writer. No other file is written for older builds, which are not expected to work with a converted repository (owner ruling, ac29 revision 2).

interactionWithShared.howDetails: The rename rule uses ArtifactIds.parse and make to turn S001 into s1 and derives EPIC, STORY and TASK ids with make; no other id is formed by hand (the single rename k2 allows).

The planner and the verifier read through ArtifactStore (read, readWithHistory, childrenOf); heads are written by the conversion-owned migration write, so the store contract is unchanged. EPIC, STORY and Task heads are created through the store.

Migrated log entries (including the review entry that carries the full report) and build rounds are appended with History.appendLog, converted and moved feedback with History.appendFeedback; entries de-duplicate by id.

Statuses are computed with the lifecycle rules and rollUp; checkHeadIntegrity and checkIntegrity must pass for every head before the marker; the revision-bearing migrated entry is the last revision-bearing entry. lifecycle.review.report uses the Review type's existing report Reference.
Uses the sidecar store for the log and feedback files and relies on its merge rules, ordering and de-duplication; the conversion commit includes the new line files.

Moves the Epic and Story bindings and attachments with bindArtifact and readBinding; the optional relabel and legacy-comment listing use the tracker port only when one is supplied and never block the marker.
Creates the Task heads of earlier Stories with TaskSets.createFromPlan, which is also the only mover of Task records; the TaskSet contract is unchanged.
Writes the marker RepoSchemaGate reads and uses RepoSchemaGate.require as the refusal at every entry point of the new tools.

errorCases.scenario: The working tree has uncommitted changes under .insrc/artifacts or docs/epics, or a merge is in progress, when a run starts
errorCases.detection: planConversion runs git status on those paths and checks for MERGE_HEAD before it reads any file
errorCases.response: Refuse with ConversionRefused naming the paths; write nothing
errorCases.userImpact: The user commits or stashes first, so the conversion's diff holds only conversion changes and reverts with one git revert

errorCases.scenario: A stored file is not valid JSON, has merge conflict markers, or has meta but no body
errorCases.detection: The planner reads raw JSON per file and records a problem instead of passing the file to the strict decoder
errorCases.response: The plan lists the file as a problem; apply refuses while any problem is open and the marker is not written
errorCases.userImpact: The user fixes or removes the file and previews again

errorCases.scenario: The tree changed between preview and apply
errorCases.detection: applyConversion recomputes the plan and compares it with the plan it was given
errorCases.response: Refuse with ConversionRefused and show what differs

errorCases.scenario: Apply stops after a migrated log entry was appended and before the head was replaced
errorCases.detection: On the rerun the planner finds the entry by its deterministic id (migrated-<artifact id>) in History.log while the head still lacks the envelope or lifecycle or still carries a legacy field
errorCases.response: The rerun appends no second entry and runs the migration write for the head only
errorCases.userImpact: A rerun finishes the head; until then the marker is absent and the new tools refuse the repository

errorCases.scenario: Apply stops before any entry was appended, or between two stamp entries
errorCases.detection: The planner finds some of the ids migrated-<artifact id>, -approve, -reject, -review, -mark-stale and not others
errorCases.response: Only the missing entries are appended, stamp and review entries first and the revision-bearing entry last, then the head is written
errorCases.userImpact: None beyond running the command again

errorCases.scenario: The migration write would change an approved head's revision number, status or approval
errorCases.detection: writeMigratedHead compares the converted head's meta.revision, lifecycle status and approval with the stored ones before the replace
errorCases.response: Refuse that head with ConversionIncomplete, write nothing for it and list it; this is a conversion bug, not a user error
errorCases.userImpact: The marker is not written and the head is named

errorCases.scenario: A head still carries a legacy field, or fails checkHeadIntegrity or checkIntegrity, after its rules ran
errorCases.detection: The post-apply sweep re-reads every head and runs both checks
errorCases.response: ConversionIncomplete lists the heads and the field or reason; the marker is not written
errorCases.userImpact: The conversion is reported unfinished; the user sees which artifacts need attention

errorCases.scenario: The after-snapshot differs from the before-snapshot for a unit (an approval is missing, a review is no longer blocking)
errorCases.detection: verifyConversion compares the planner's legacyDeliveryView snapshot with the snapshot the delivery reader builds from the lifecycle of the converted heads
errorCases.response: Report each difference with the unit and the reason; never correct it; a contentHash difference is expected and not reported
errorCases.userImpact: The user decides whether a difference is expected

errorCases.scenario: The conversion is run before the delivery readers were moved to the lifecycle
errorCases.detection: verifyConversion reads the converted heads through the delivery reader and finds no approval on any approved unit; apply checks, before it starts, that the delivery reader's approval source is the lifecycle (a build-time guard in the plan: the reader group is a precondition)
errorCases.response: Refuse to apply with ConversionRefused naming the unmoved reader
errorCases.userImpact: The reader group is finished first

errorCases.scenario: A review report cannot be placed (the review stamp has no verdict, or its findings are malformed)
errorCases.detection: The lifecycle back-fill validates the stored report the way the delivery gate does and drops malformed findings into the report's own list of dropped values
errorCases.response: The review entry carries the report as stored plus the dropped values; the lifecycle gets the verdict only when it is valid; the report counts these heads

errorCases.scenario: An uppercase story id would rename onto an existing file or onto another rename's target
errorCases.detection: The planner builds the rename map first and checks every target name against existing files and other renames
errorCases.response: A collision is a problem in the plan and no rename is applied
errorCases.userImpact: The user resolves the collision by hand

errorCases.scenario: A reference to a renamed id sits where the planner cannot rewrite it (free text, an issue body on the tracker)
errorCases.detection: After the rename map is built, the planner searches heads and docs for each old id
errorCases.response: References in structured fields are rewritten; references in prose are listed in the report and left as they are
errorCases.userImpact: The report names each remaining place

errorCases.scenario: The optional tracker step fails (no gh access, rate limit, the issue was deleted)
errorCases.detection: The tracker port returns a failed PortResult
errorCases.response: Record the failure in the report with the issue and the reason; do not block the marker; the next run retries
errorCases.userImpact: A possible duplicate issue is accepted until the step succeeds, as the s1 hand-off says

errorCases.scenario: Pre-s8 'Attached ...' comments exist on a bound issue
errorCases.detection: With a tracker port supplied, the planner lists the issue's comments and matches the legacy attach shape (no insrc marker)
errorCases.response: They are listed in legacyAttachComments and in the report; nothing is rewritten or deleted and no reader recognises them
errorCases.userImpact: The first comment sync records each as a person's comment; the owner may delete them on the issue first

errorCases.scenario: A legacy review is dated before the head's current revision, or reviewResolutions contradict the stored verdict
errorCases.detection: The lifecycle back-fill applies the same rule as effectiveReviewVerdict and the gate's mirror: a review older than the revision is not bound to it
errorCases.response: The lifecycle gets no review for that head and the report counts it under unbound reviews; the review entry still records the report
errorCases.userImpact: The other-party review gate asks for a new review, as it would have before

errorCases.scenario: A body.feedback entry has an author that is not a namespaced id, or a target.file that is not the artifact's own document
errorCases.detection: convertLegacyFeedback inspects the author text and the target
errorCases.response: The author becomes legacy:<slug> with the text in actor.properties.name; a foreign file goes to anchor.section; both are counted in the report

errorCases.scenario: A new tool runs on an unconverted repository
errorCases.detection: RepoSchemaGate.require(repo, 2) at the entry of each daemon method and MCP step
errorCases.response: Return the message that names the conversion and repo.convert
errorCases.userImpact: A clear refusal instead of a decoder error

errorCases.scenario: A step of persistReview fails (the fix is stored, the lifecycle review is not)
errorCases.detection: persistReview wraps each of its steps and records which completed
errorCases.response: ReviewPersistError names the failed step and what is stored; the lifecycle record comes before the markdown, so a rerun repairs the rest
errorCases.userImpact: The reviewer sees which step to repeat

The plan is held in memory; the report prints counts and the first problems, the full list is in the result

invariantsToPreserve.text: A revision moves only when content changes: the conversion keeps every head's meta.revision, status and approval as stored, and only the contentHash (of the converted content) changes (k3; src/workflow/storage.ts reconciles the hash on a content write, which is why the store is not the write path)
Approval and review bind to a revision number, not to a hash, so the new contentHash does not unbind them (src/workflow/artifact-core/lifecycle.ts)

The delivery reader reads one shape after the reader group is done: the lifecycle; the legacy stamp rules live only in the conversion's legacyDeliveryView and go with it (src/workflow/delivery/load.ts approvalOf is the behaviour that is reproduced once)
An artifact id never changes once created, except the single rename of an uppercase story id to lowercase by this conversion (k2)
The marker is written last and only when every head passes the head and log integrity checks, so a half-converted repository is refused by the new tools
The conversion is repeatable: every rule tests the stored state and every migrated log entry has a deterministic id, so a second run writes nothing
Feedback entries are immutable and append-only; converting or copying them stores each id once (the sidecar reader de-duplicates by id)
Folder names under docs/epics stay as they are (k7)
The daemon owns all file access; the command is an IPC method and the CLI only calls it

migration.stateBefore: Repository at schema version 1 (no .insrc/schema.json). Heads carry the legacy stamps (meta.approvedAt, rejectedAt, rejectReason, reviewOverride, staleAckedAt, review, reviewResolutions) beside or instead of meta.lifecycle; body.feedback holds pre-s5 feedback; the Epic and Story bindings and attachments sit on the Define and the LLD; a Story's tracker feedback lines and receipts sit on the LLD; the Plan keeps the Task tracker records; no EPIC, STORY, TASKS or TASK heads exist for Stories planned before s7; AMD files are flat records; 444 files carry uppercase S0nn ids. The delivery reader derives approval and review only from the legacy stamps (src/workflow/delivery/load.ts approvalOf, gate.ts, currency.ts). A content write through ArtifactStore moves meta.revision and returns the head to draft when the content hash changes (src/workflow/storage.ts). The gates still write the legacy fields while the readers read them (s1 bundles 'how a head is written', 'the delivery reader derives approval and review only from the legacy stamps', 'the legacy stamp surface after s1-s8, by role', 'the lifecycle Review keeps only a summary of a review', 'tracker records, story history and feedback that move or go').
migration.stateAfter: Repository at schema version 2. Every head has meta.envelope and meta.lifecycle with the revision number, status and approval it had, a contentHash of the converted content, a revision-bearing migrated log entry (migrated-<artifact id>), stamp entries that record the legacy approval, rejection and stale marks, and a review entry that carries the full review report and resolutions (lifecycle.review.report references it). Feedback is in sidecar lines with namespaced actors; EPIC, STORY, TASKS and TASK heads exist and hold the bindings, attachments, tracker feedback lines and receipts; AMD records are heads; ids are lowercase. The legacy stamps, meta.review, the body.feedback writers, the Plan Task records and the head-less fallbacks are gone from heads and production code; the delivery reader and every other reader read the lifecycle; LifecycleService is the only approval path; persistReview is the one review path; new tools refuse a repository without the marker.

migrationSteps.action: Build the conversion engine behind the daemon method repo.convert (default mode preview): the planner with legacyDeliveryView, the per-rule converters, the migration write, the applier, the verifier and the marker writer. Change convertLegacyFeedback to the s5 mapping. Add readReviewReport and persistReview. Nothing is switched on for a repository yet.

Move the readers to the lifecycle, delivery readers first (load, gate, currency, types), then pending, admit, chain, artifact-content, completion-evidence, the tracker readers, party, workflow-rpc, access, mcp server and cli service; the review readers use readReviewReport. Update the write inventory for findings.ts. This group is a precondition of the first run of the conversion.

Move the writers and gates to LifecycleService and delete the stamps (STAMP_KEYS, mirrorLegacyReview, headConflict becomes the full log check); findings, verdicts and run-artifact call persistReview; make LifecycleService mandatory.

Remove body.feedback writers and the tool artifact_feedback_append; remove the Plan Task record readers, bindingHome's Plan fallback, taskBuildPassed's BUILD-record branch and the older tracker refs (epicRef, storyRef, storyRefs, taskRefs, units); point artifactOfUnit at the STORY head; render the PLAN task table from the Task heads; add the RepoSchemaGate.require guards at each daemon method and MCP step (repo.convert is exempt).

Run the Story's full test sweep and build, code-review and approve the BUILD with the previous daemon still running; the daemon that drives the build keeps its old code until it is restarted, so the build tooling is not refused by its own guards.

Restart the daemon on the new code, then on a clean working tree run preview and read the plan: renames, problems, unmapped values, reviews that cannot be bound, prose references to renamed ids, legacy attach comments.

Run apply. Rules run in order: rename uppercase ids and files; stamp epicCreatedAt; convert flat amendments; for each head, under the artifact's lock, append the missing migrated log entries (stamp and review entries first, the revision-bearing entry last) and then replace the head with the migration write; convert body.feedback; create EPIC and STORY heads; create Task heads for earlier Stories through TaskSets.createFromPlan and back-fill build rounds; move the Epic and Story bindings and attachments; move story history; strip the legacy fields. The working tree is left changed.

Run the post-apply sweep: every head decodes, carries no legacy field and passes checkHeadIntegrity and checkIntegrity, and every approved head has its stored revision number, status and approval. Only then write .insrc/schema.json (version 2) by temporary file and rename.
Run verify: the before-snapshot the planner computed from the legacy stamps against the snapshot the delivery reader builds from the converted repository; print each difference.
Optional, with a tracker: relabel and retitle old issues so the create guard recognises them and list the pre-s8 attach comments; report failures.
Commit the result as one commit (the data changes, the new line files and the marker). Reverting it with git revert returns the tree to version 1 for the tools of the previous release.

migration.backwardCompat: None is kept in the new tools: a repository without the marker is refused, and the old shapes are not read after this Story. Builds from before this model are not expected to work with a converted repository (the owner's ruling, recorded in docs/plans/core-data-model.md and in ac29 revision 2 of the DEF); no notice file or compatibility reader is added. The IPC method names are unchanged; repo.convert is added; artifact_feedback_append and the legacy-stamp parameters of the gates are removed.

alternativesConsidered.name: Conversion engine with its own migration write and planner-side before-snapshot
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A planner, an applier, a verifier and a marker writer in src/workflow/convert; heads are written by a conversion-owned migration write that keeps revision, status and approval as stored; the before-snapshot is computed from the raw legacy heads and the after-snapshot is read with the real delivery reader.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new module src/workflow/convert holds planConversion, applyConversion, verifyConversion and a migration writer. The planner reads raw JSON files (not through the strict decoder), returns a typed list of changes per artifact, and computes the BEFORE snapshot with a pure conversion-owned function legacyDeliveryView over the legacy stamps (status, revision number, approval, review verdict, blocking, open feedback count). The applier runs the rules in a fixed order. For each head it takes ArtifactStore.exclusive, appends the missing migrated log entries with deterministic ids (migrated-<artifact id>-approve, -reject, -review, -mark-stale, then the revision-bearing migrated-<artifact id>) through History.appendLog, then replaces the head with the migration write. The migration write builds meta.envelope and meta.lifecycle, strips the legacy body and meta fields, keeps meta.revision, status and approval as stored, sets revision.contentHash to the hash of the converted content, sets lifecycle.review.report to a Reference to the review change-log entry (which carries the full review report and resolutions as outcome.data), and writes by writeAtomic; it appends nothing. EPIC and STORY heads, Task heads (TaskSets.createFromPlan, which also moves the Plan's Task record), the Epic and Story bindings and the Story history are created or moved by the same applier. The AFTER snapshot is read with the real delivery reader, which by then reads the lifecycle only, because the reader move is ordered before the first run of the conversion; the new tools refuse an unconverted repository and repo.convert is exempt. The marker is written last, only when every head passes the integrity checks. The retirement of the legacy stamps and fallbacks is a separate, ordered group of changes in the same Story.
pros: No change to the sc2 store contract, so no HLD amendment
Revision, status and approval survive the conversion because the store's content-write rule is never applied
The before and after snapshots use no dual-shape reader, so no compatibility code remains
A rerun is safe: each rule tests stored state and every migrated entry has a deterministic id
A preview is the planner alone
cons: A second code path writes heads (the migration write), so it needs its own checks that mirror the store's invariants
legacyDeliveryView must reproduce the old reader's approval and review rules, and is a copy of that logic used once
It writes under ArtifactStore.exclusive but not through the store's journal, so a crash between the entry and the head is repaired by a rerun
Large: the engine and the retirement work are both in one Story

alternativesConsidered.name: Add a migrate method to ArtifactStore and a dual-shape delivery reader
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The store gets a migration write of its own (added to sc2 by an amendment) and the delivery reader reads both the legacy stamps and the lifecycle, so the snapshots use the one reader.
alternativesConsidered.approach: ArtifactStore gains migrate(a, by, options) that writes the envelope and lifecycle and the stripped body without moving the revision, through the same staged operation and journal as write, with a caller-chosen operation id (a sharedContract.methodAdd amendment on sc2). The delivery reader gains a mode that reads the lifecycle when a head has one and the legacy stamps otherwise, so the same reader produces the before and after snapshots. The rest follows a1.
pros: One writer of heads, with the journal giving crash repair for free
One delivery reader for both snapshots, no copied logic
cons: Changes a contract another Story owns (sc2) and needs an approved amendment first
Keeps the legacy stamp reading in the delivery reader, which is the compatibility code the owner ruled out
Reopens the staged-operation code that s4 owns
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Equal on the criteria but partial on sc2 and sc5, and it keeps a dual-shape delivery reader the owner ruled out.

alternativesConsidered.name: Write through the store and re-approve
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use ArtifactStore.write for every converted head and accept that stripped bodies move revisions and return heads to draft; approvals are re-granted by script.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The converter calls ArtifactStore.write with the converted artifact. Because the body changes, the store moves meta.revision and sets the head to draft; the conversion then re-applies each recorded approval and review through LifecycleService.apply with the migration actor.
pros: The store's journal and log rules are used as they are
cons: Breaks k3 (a revision moves only when content changes by a person) and rewrites the history of every approved artifact
Approvals become migration approvals by a system actor, not the people who gave them
A stripped feedback list would address open feedback unless addresses is passed on every call
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smallest, but violates k3, k5 and sc4.
